scope_reason: The Tainted One is immune to all poisons, an individual immunity against the opponent's poisoned attacks.

reviewed_clause_text: Wheelos count as henchmen, but whenever they earn an advancement, they instead roll on the Hero's Advancement Table (in that regard, they're very much like Hired Swords). reviewed_clause_text: This Goblin can ride one of the warband's Cave Squigs, or even a Great Squig! The pair deploy as a single model. Standard mount rules are not used, although the rider counts as being mounted for the Cavelry Bonus rule (see spears and lances). While the Squig is being ridden, it and the rider move as a single model using the Squig's movement rules, but attack separately in Close Combat. In this skill's text, the use of “Squig” refers to both Cave Squigs and Great Squigs. Any shooting or close combat attacks will hit the rider on a D6 roll of 1-2, and the Squig on a 3-6. If the Squig is stunned or taken out of action, the rider takes a Strength 2 hit with no Armour save as they crash to the ground. If the Rider is stunned or taken out of action, the Squig reverts to normal Squig behavior. In either case the rider is now dismounted for the rest of the battle. Squigs don't like being ridden. If the movement roll results in a double or triple, the rider must roll a D6 before the Squig moves. If the result is over the rider's Strength, they are thrown off before the Squig moves away, and take a Strength 2 hit with no Armour save as they crash to the ground. The rider is now dismounted for the rest of the battle. If the roll is equal to or below their Strength, the rider keeps their grip and remains atop the Squig.
scope_reason: The clause forms rider and Cave Squig into a pair that deploys as one model but attacks separately, allocates each attack between rider and mount on a D6, and can throw and injure the rider. That is an additional independent combatant with its own attacks and profile, which the duel excludes, and the mounting/movement/throw-off sentences are movement rules.

reviewed_clause_text: When the hero with Stampede charges an opposing warrior, keep track of any other Snotlings that charged that same warrior this turn. reviewed_clause_text: The statline above represents the stats of the Wheelo's Crew members, who pull out built-in weapons and hide behind wooden armour. If the Wheelo rolls into an opponent, it counts as a charge, and the crew will fight in each hand-to-hand combat phase as normal. If the Wheelo is charged by an opponent, they will likewise fight, although without the Impact Hit bonus. If the Wheelo accidentally rolls into a friendly model, that model suffers Impact Hits (see above), but the crew will not attack the model. If the Wheelo rolls into a Fear-causing opponent, it still counts as a charge (and the model still suffers Impact Hits), but the crew must pass a Leadership Test, otherwise they will not hit on anything but 6s.
scope_reason: The Wheelo crew fighting each phase, counting a roll-into as a charge without the impact bonus when charged, and testing Leadership against a Fear-causing opponent are admitted attack, charge and individual psychology consequences.

reviewed_clause_text: Whenever a Wheelo moves into a model, that model automatically suffers 1D3 Strength 4 hits, which are worked out before any blows are struck, in the same way as a crossbow pistol. These represent the Impact Hits of the Wheelo as it comes to a sudden stop against an unsolid object. These are only dealt in the first round of combat, and only if the Wheelo "charged" this turn. Models that charge a Wheelo during his or her turn do NOT suffer Impact Hits. If a Wheelo rolls into a friendly model, that model still suffers Impact Hits as normal. An Impact Hit does not reflect the strength of the Wheelo crew, and thus the attack will remain S4, even if the crew gains a Strength Upgrade.

reviewed_clause_text: A Wheelo's movement is entirely dependent upon the efforts of the Snotling crew to give it enough speed to move. Walking: a Wheelo has a move of 1D6 inches, rolled each turn that it walks; it may only ever move in a straight line forwards or backwards, but may pivot up to 90 degrees on the spot before moving. If the Wheelo collides into any form of terrain other than open terrain, or comes into base-to-base contact with a building's wall, the machine immediately stops (note: this enables climbing to take place - though it's still random climbing so if you get halfway up the wall only, you fall as normal). If the 1D6" move brings the Wheelo into another model, it deals Impact Hits to it - if the model was an enemy, it counts as a charge. Running/Charging: instead of only moving 1D6", a Wheelo may instead run or charge 2D6". If this brings it into contact with an enemy, it counts as a charge; if the move falls short, the Wheelo's move is NOT halved, like normal failed charges. Every time a running/charging Wheelo moves over/through a different piece of terrain (open terrain such as streets etc. has no penalties, but moving over difficult terrain such as rubble, barricades, and into houses etc. would incur the damage rolls), the Wheelo takes an automatic Strength 5 hit, worked out immediately when the Wheelo contacts the piece of terrain.
scope_reason: The whole entry is Wheelo movement: walking and running dice, pivoting, stopping at terrain, climbing, and terrain damage during runs; movement, terrain and distance are excluded from the duel.

If no such charge is possible but the Goblin can shoot, it shoots the nearest eligible friendly target. reviewed_clause_text: At the start of each battle nominate one of your opponent's Female warriors as the Pimp's mark. Treat this like a Bounty Hunter's mark, except that instead of earning a reward after the battle has ended, the mark is captured by the Pimp. The Pimp gets +1 to hit his mark and must always move towards them. He gains +D3 Experience for each mark he puts out of action if he survives and the battle was won. After the battle do not roll on the Serious Injuries chart, marks count as captured. Any weapons can be kept by the warband or sold.
scope_reason: The +1 to hit the nominated mark is an admitted individual attack consequence, with the opposing profile supplied as a current condition.
notes: The nomination, capture, Experience and post-battle halves of the same printed rule are campaign procedures and are excluded from this decision.

scope_reason: The dagger, throwing-knife and stiletto armament, the no-armour bar and the Haggle and Streetwise skills of the Trickster-Priest are admitted construction clauses of this profile.

reviewed_clause_text: The Priestess gains an eagle companion each time she acquires this mark. Eagles are weapons she directs: in close combat they strike first, use her Weapon Skill, and each successful attack inflicts a Strength 3 hit. Eagles cannot be attacked or slain and fly away when the Priestess is taken out of action. Their 24-inch shooting attack and post-battle return/loss are outside the resolved melee duel.
scope_reason: The directable eagle companion whose close-combat attacks strike first at the Priestess' Weapon Skill for a Strength 3 hit is an admitted individual attack consequence of this duelist.
notes: The acquisition of the mark, the 24-inch shooting attack and the post-battle return or loss of the eagle are excluded and are not part of this decision.

reviewed_clause_text: Divine purpose washes over the Priest; he automatically passes all Leadership based tests taken while fighting against Orcs & Goblins or the followers of Chaos.
scope_reason: Automatically passing Leadership-based tests while fighting Orcs and Goblins or followers of Chaos is an admitted individual Leadership rule of this duelist.

reviewed_clause_text: Enemy warriors from Witch Hunters, Sisters of Sigmar or mercenary warbands except Marienburg/Middenheim, within 3 inches of the Priest, suffer -1 on all rolls to hit when attacking a warrior within 3 inches of him.
scope_reason: The -1 to hit suffered by the named enemy warriors attacking within 3 inches of the Priest is admitted as an explicit current condition on the opposing duelist, generating no surrounding group.

reviewed_clause_text: Whalers grow accustomed to hunting marine beasts. Double any wounds inflicted to aquatic models.
scope_reason: Doubling the wounds inflicted on aquatic models is an admitted individual attack consequence of this duelist with the opposing profile supplied as a current condition.

reviewed_clause_text: Wolf-Priests of Ulric may never wear armour, trusting in Ulric's protection. The only exception is that every Wolf-Priest is garbed in a cloak made from the pelt of a white wolf; the pelt allows a 6+ saving throw. Black powder weapons, crossbows and helmets are not favoured by Ulric; use of them shows a lack of courage. Wolf-Priests of Ulric may never be equipped with blackpowder weapons.
scope_reason: The no-armour bar with the white wolf pelt exception and its 6+ save, and the blackpowder bar, are admitted construction and defence clauses of this profile.

reviewed_clause_text: The Priest suffers -1 Ballistic Skill, can fight unarmed without the usual penalties and cannot be disarmed, and is immune to harmful cold except when triggered by magic.
scope_reason: Fighting unarmed without the usual penalties, being immune to disarmament and the -1 Ballistic Skill are admitted individual facts of this duelist.
notes: The cold immunity concerns weather, which the duel boundary excludes; the Ballistic Skill reduction has no effect in the melee duel but is retained as a profile change.

reviewed_clause_text: Extra equipment cannot normally be bought for a Hired Sword and the Hired Sword's equipment cannot be sold by the warband.
scope_reason: The fixed, non-transferable equipment of a Hired Sword is an admitted construction clause of these profiles.
notes: The bans on buying extra equipment and on selling the kit belong to the campaign market, which the duel boundary excludes.
